svg.title: The ways to choose where bots run
svg.desc: Three working ways: everything on this Mac; a server over SSH, where the app opens the port forward itself; a server by address, where you forward the port and paste the access key. A fourth, a ready-made server, is a placeholder that does nothing.

text.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Everything runs on your Mac. The app reads the access key from the bridge's own file.

svg.text: 2 A server I reach over SSH

text.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The app runs the system ssh, keeps the forward open, and reads the access key from the server's file.

svg.text: 3 A server by address and access key

text.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: You forward the port yourself, with the same number on both ends, and paste the access key.

svg.text: 4 Get a ready-made server from us

text.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Shown in the setup window as “Coming soon”. It does nothing: no server is created and nothing is sent.

svg.text: The bridge answers on loopback only, so a server is always reached through a forward of its port.
